paper_id: Zhu et al. - 2007 - Low-Power Distributed Event Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks
title: Low-Power Distributed Event Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: Tiny sensor nodes have limited energy; duty cycling saves energy but degrades event detection performance
problem_framing: Quantify tradeoffs between detection delay/detectability and network lifetime in low duty-cycled WSNs
key_insight: Neighboring sensors should evenly separate wakeup times to minimize detection delay variance
method_signature: CAS: distributed cooperative wakeup scheduling via variance reduction of wakeup separations
evaluation_criteria: Detection delay (mean/std), detectability percentage, tradeoff with network lifetime
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: The theoretical lower bounds are over optimistic and can never be achieved in reality
evidence_for_taste: it is apparent for applications that smaller delay and higher detectability are more preferable
